solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S014-01.notes: Laying out every explanation without taking a side = noncommittal. 'Ambivalent' (mixed feelings) is the attractive trap; 'indifferent' implies lack of care, contradicted by 'meticulously'; 'partisan' is the opposite.

flags: minor: key is the only unfamiliar/high-register word; test-takers can reach it by eliminating three clearly wrong familiar words
S014-02.notes: Dense allusions to obscure texts that few could follow = recondite (obscure). Derivative contradicts the contrast with imitated early work; accessible is the opposite; prolific is irrelevant.

S014-03.notes: Claim is about the size of B's advantage: rural 73-64=9 vs urban 75-72=3. Only A compares the gaps; arithmetic checks.

S014-04.notes: Bees remembered and returned to caffeinated flowers, so caffeine encourages repeat visits that aid pollination. Other choices contradict the findings.

flags: Tests the contested 'one of the few X who have/has' construction. Prescriptively the relative clause modifies the plural 'biologists', so 'have' is correct, but 'has' is very common in edited prose and is defended by some usage guides; the official SAT generally avoids testing this disputed point. Consider rewriting so the antecedent is unambiguous (e.g., 'Dr. Osei, unlike most marine biologists, ______ observed...').
S014-05.notes: Antecedent of 'who' is 'marine biologists' (plural), so 'have'. Most quick solvers will pick 'has' to agree with Dr. Osei. 'Having' and 'is having' create no finite verb / wrong aspect.

S014-06.notes: 'that' introduces a noun clause object of 'argued'; no punctuation between verb and object clause or after 'that'.

S014-07.notes: Infants learning language sounds in an early window parallels songbirds' sensitive period: 'Similarly'. Not a contrast, cause, or example of the songbird finding.

flags: minor: D is the only choice that mentions scientists or doubt, mirroring the goal's 'surprised scientists' wording directly
S014-08.notes: Surprise requires pairing the doubt about tiny birds' fat storage with the 6,000 km migration; only D combines both.

S014-09.notes: Last sentence: the note rang clearly (progress) and she feared the next might not (fear it won't last). A, C, D unsupported.

S014-10.notes: Economist points to a simultaneous confounder (lower speed limits), so she'd say the drop may be partly due to that change. A and C contradict her; B ignores her point.
